addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

attachment.content:
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### 5. ПРАВИЛА РАБОТЫ, ВЫВЕДЕННЫЕ ЗА СМЕНУ

- **Кто держит длинное.** Полный набор тестов (двадцать минут) гоняет координатор фоновой
  задачей. У исполнителя есть потолок в десять минут на один вызов инструмента — длинную
  цепь гейтов он не может удержать в одном ходу, обвязка сама уводит её в фон и ход
  заканчивается пустым ответом. Улика: агент `a958ef6bcfb0b7018` в 13:29 IDT потерял так
  результат полного прогона.
- **Что гоняет исполнитель.** Быстрый сухой прогон `bash guardrails/pre-push < /dev/null`
  (минута-две, все гейты кроме набора тестов) плюс узкие тесты по своим файлам, последним
  шагом. Это тот же самый набор гейтов, что видит настоящий пуш — не «похожий», а буквально
  тот же код, доказано: `guardrails/pre-push` не делает сетевых вызовов
  (`grep -rn "git push\|git fetch\|curl\|wget\|ssh"` — пусто), и оба пути читают один и тот
  же диапазон `origin/main..HEAD`.
- **Классификатор охвата пуша исправен.** `guardrails/check-push-reach.sh` верно сказал
  «FULL» по всем трём сегодняшним поломкам заранее. Их причиной был собственный запрет
  координатора гонять полный набор, взятый из хендоффа №4 и растянутый шире, чем там
  написано — не дефект машины.
- **Чем проверяют защиту.** Доказывать, что хук или сторож работает, нужно ПОДАВАЯ ему
  строку команды, а не выполняя команду по-настоящему. Проверка защиты не должна делать
  того, от чего защищает. Родилось из случая: агент, строивший хук против `git clean -f`,
  доказывал его тест реальным `git clean -fn` в песочнице — холостая форма, но настоящая
  команда, и сторож транскриптов поймал её как боевую (увидел `-f`, не увидел `-n`).
- **Почему нельзя ставить хуки из рабочей копии в стороне (ланы), пока рядом идёт чужая
  доставка.** У связанной рабочей копии хуки живут в ОБЩЕМ каталоге главной копии
  (`guardrails/install.sh:16-18`: `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` ведёт в общий каталог из
  любой копии). Улика: исполнитель поставил свой изменённый `guardrails/pre-push` в общий
  `.git/hooks/pre-push` в 14:09 IDT — тот вызывал скрипт, которого не было ни у одной
  соседней копии, и доставка встала у всех соседей разом («can't open file
  .../guardrails/check-gates-manifest.py»). Свой гейт проверяется сухим прогоном ИЗ СВОЕГО
  дерева — он берёт файл своей копии, а не установленный.
- **Кто перенумеровывается при столкновении номеров.** Правило: ДВИГАЕТСЯ ТО, ЧТО НЕ УЕХАЛО.
  Строка, уже стоящая в main, номера не меняет — на неё уже могут ссылаться записи прувера и
  чужие ветки. Перенумеровывается та ветка, что ещё не слилась, и берёт номер с запасом от
  максимума по всему дереву, включая архив. Причина правила — чистое слияние может испортить
  дерево, даже без единого конфликт-маркера: `check-matrix-reference.py` сверяет тело со
  справочником, но не уникальность номеров, и дал «OK» при задвоенных `M-547`/`M-548`/строке
  очереди 625 после слияния без конфликтов. Лечение — отдельный тест уникальности
  (`tests/test_row_id_uniqueness.py`), не новый гейт: гейт потребовал бы записи в едином доме
  устройства, тест дешевле.
- **Почему сторож обязан проверять, что файл ещё разбирается.** Гейт `af` сверял смысл
  формулировок в `.github/workflows/gates.yml`, но ни разу не спросил, разбирается ли файл

SRC="$ROOT/hooks/worker-restore-guard.py"
DEST_DIR="$HOME/.claude/hooks"
DEST="$DEST_DIR/worker-restore-guard.py"
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"

if [ -f "$DEST" ] && cmp -s "$SRC" "$DEST"; then
  echo "already present: $DEST"
else
  cp "$SRC" "$DEST"
  chmod +x "$DEST"
  echo "installed: $DEST"
fi

python3 - "$SETTINGS" <<'PY'
import json, os, sys

settings_path = sys.argv[1]
cmd = "python3 ~/.claude/hooks/worker-restore-guard.py"
fname = "worker-restore-guard.py"

s = json.load(open(settings_path)) if os.path.isfile(settings_path) else {}
pre = s.setdefault("hooks", {}).setdefault("PreToolUse", [])
have = [h.get("command", "") for entry in pre for h in entry.get("hooks", [])]
if any(fname in c for c in have):
    print("already wired: PreToolUse hook %s" % fname)
else:
    pre.append({"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": cmd}]})
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(settings_path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(settings_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(s, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write("\n")
    print("wired: PreToolUse hook %s -> %s" % (fname, settings_path))

# law allows, silent on a quoted mention.
deny1=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git stash push -q tests/x.py"}}' \
        | python3 "$DEST")
deny2=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo hi && git checkout -- ."}}' \
        | python3 "$DEST")
quiet1=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git checkout main"}}' \
         | python3 "$DEST")
quiet2=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git restore --staged x.py"}}' \
         | python3 "$DEST")
quiet3=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git stash list"}}' \
         | python3 "$DEST")
quiet4=$(printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo \"git stash\""}}' \
         | python3 "$DEST")

case "$deny1" in *deny*) : ;; *) echo "self-test FAILED: git stash push not denied"; exit 1;; esac
case "$deny2" in *deny*) : ;; *) echo "self-test FAILED: second-position git checkout -- not denied"; exit 1;; esac
[ -z "$quiet1" ] || { echo "self-test FAILED: git checkout <branch> wrongly denied"; exit 1; }
[ -z "$quiet2" ] || { echo "self-test FAILED: git restore --staged wrongly denied"; exit 1; }
[ -z "$quiet3" ] || { echo "self-test FAILED: git stash list wrongly denied"; exit 1; }
[ -z "$quiet4" ] || { echo "self-test FAILED: quoted mention wrongly denied"; exit 1; }
echo "self-tests OK: the five forbidden forms deny (plain and second-position); allowed forms and quoted mentions pass"
echo "Installed. Every new Bash call this session hands to a shell is checked first; a worker or the seat handing one of the five forms to a shell now gets refused instead of run."

You are a worker on the live-spec project. Work ONLY inside the worktree /private/tmp/live-spec-hands/wt — never touch any other directory, never touch ~/live-spec, never touch ~/.claude.

HARD BOUNDARIES (violating these fails the task): no `git reset`, no `git rebase`, no `git stash`, no `git clean`, no `git checkout -- <path>`, no `git push`. Do not commit — leave your changes in the working tree and report. Do not run the full pytest suite (it takes 20 minutes and the coordinator runs it); run only the narrow tests you touch.

THE DEFECT TO FIX (real, just observed):
`guardrails/check-config-health.sh` (gate m) reds when an installed hook is missing from ~/.claude/hooks, and prints this advice in its JSON finding:
  "fix":"run scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh or scripts/install-session-hooks.sh"
(line 59, and a similar line 84 for a drifted hook).

That advice is FALSE for at least one hook. `hooks/worker-restore-guard.py` is installed by neither of those two scripts — it has its own installer, `scripts/install-worker-restore-guard.sh`. A person who read the gate's advice, ran `sh scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh`, and looked again would find the gate still red and the advice exhausted. This was hit for real today.

YOUR JOB:
1. Read `guardrails/check-config-health.sh` fully first, and read `scripts/install-pack-hooks.sh`, `scripts/install-session-hooks.sh`, and `scripts/install-worker-restore-guard.sh` to learn which hook filenames each one actually ships.
2. Make the gate's advice name the installer that actually carries the hook it is complaining about. Prefer the honest mechanical route: derive the answer from the scripts themselves (e.g. grep the installer scripts for the hook's filename) rather than hard-coding a second name in prose — a hard-coded list would drift the same way the current advice drifted. If a hook is carried by no installer at all, the advice must say that plainly rather than naming a script that will not help.
3. Keep the JSON finding shape exactly as it is (same keys: severity, code, message, fix) — other machinery reads it.
4. Add or extend a test proving the new behaviour, in the existing test file that covers this check if one exists (look for tests naming config-health, e.g. `grep -rln "config-health" tests/`). The test must be red-first in spirit: it must fail against the old advice text and pass against the new. Follow the surrounding test file's own style exactly.
5. Verify: run `sh guardrails/check-config-health.sh` (it should still print OK on this machine) and run the narrow test file you touched with `python3 -m pytest <file> -q`.

STYLE RULES OF THIS PROJECT (they are enforced by gates, take them seriously):
- Prose in comments and messages is plain English, one idea per sentence, no jargon, no marketing tone.
- Never use CAPITAL LETTERS for emphasis. Technical values go in backticks, not in capitals.
- Do not leave a queue row number standing where plain words belong — name what a thing is, not just its number.

REPORT BACK (this is your return value, keep it under 30 lines): which files you changed and how, the exact new advice text, the test you added and its name, and the pasted output of the two verification commands. If you concluded the fix should take a different shape than described above, say so and explain with evidence.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# open-lane.sh — the lane-open act (SPEC INV-214, T-23, E-34).
#
# Opening a parallel build lane is a step the session PERFORMS, not narration it
# emits. This script is that step's performable form. It runs the concrete git
# ceremony the branch road specifies: the row→in-work claim commit on main under
# the pen, the lane branch cut from that commit into its own worktree, and the
# worker brief stub that names the branch the lane rides.
#
# Usage:
#   1. Edit the queue (ROADMAP.md): flip the row's status cell to in-work, and
#      STAGE only that file  (git add ROADMAP.md).
#   2. scripts/open-lane.sh <row-number> <slug>
#   3. Delegate the lane to a worker with the Agent tool's isolation: "worktree"
#      option (it carries no gate), the brief naming the printed branch.
#
# Preconditions it enforces — each a red that stops the act:
#   - run from the PRIMARY worktree on main, so the claim commit lands where INV-2's
#     ancestry order can read it (a claim on a lane's own branch sits outside it);
#   - the row→in-work flip staged, and ONLY the queue file staged, so the claim
#     commit carries one row's delta (INV-39);
#   - the profile cap not exceeded: open lanes + 1 <= lanes.cap (default 3, INV-214/T-18);
#   - the fence unbroken where it is armed (INV-11);
#   - the lane branch not already present.
#
# Env overrides (for tests and non-default hosts):
#   LIVE_SPEC_QUEUE       the queue file the claim commit carries      (default ROADMAP.md)
#   LIVE_SPEC_PROFILE     the profile the cap is read from             (default ~/.claude/live-spec/profile.md)
#   LIVE_SPEC_WORKTREES   the base dir the lane worktree is created in (default .claude/worktrees)
set -euo pipefail

die() { echo "open-lane: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

[ $# -eq 2 ] || die "usage: open-lane.sh <row-number> <slug>"
ROW="$1"; SLUG="$2"
[[ "$ROW" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "row must be a number, got '$ROW'"
[[ "$SLUG" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]] || die "slug must be kebab-case [a-z0-9-], got '$SLUG'"

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die "not inside a git repo"
cd "$ROOT"

Every current consumer of `ARCHITECTURE.md` — `guardrails/check-pin-drift.sh:49`, `guardrails/node_growth_counter.py:90`, `guardrails/crosscut_counter.py:120`, `guardrails/check-prover-record.sh:251` — hardcodes a single `ARCHITECTURE.md` path; none call `spec_paths`/`read_document` (`grep -n "parts\|spec_paths\|read_document"` across those files returns nothing but an unrelated string match). `tests/conftest.py`'s `read()` (line ~111) special-cases only `SPEC` and `MATRIX`; `ARCHITECTURE.md` falls through to a plain `open().read()`. So: confirmed, and the plumbing genuinely does not exist for architecture.

**Claim 2 (no single generated `## Reference`; nine sections instead) — CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated.**
`grep -n '^## ' ARCHITECTURE.md` shows 11 top-level headings; after `## Nodes` (line 42-613) come exactly nine: Seams, Feature coverage, Runtime view, Placement view, Footprint and proof by project.kind, Design principles by project.kind, Composition axes by project.kind, Quality budgets, Decisions — where they live (lines 614-916). None of them is script-generated: `scripts/` has only `build-index.py` (spec) and `build-matrix-reference.py` (matrix), no `build-architecture*.py`; `guardrails/check-index-generated.py` is wired to `specformat` only. Reading all nine sections in full (`ARCHITECTURE.md:600-916`) shows narrative prose in every table cell, including a hand-typed history of seven suite-timing measurements in "Quality budgets" — the opposite of mechanical output. `tests/test_traceability.py:2933-3184` parses "Feature coverage" by string-splitting the raw file, i.e. it *checks* the hand-written table two-way, it doesn't regenerate it. | Section | Kind | How determined |
|---|---|---|
| Preamble + Shape at a glance | hand-written | prose, no table, no builder script referencing it |
| Nodes | hand-written, per-field-checked | `archformat.py` parses/validates shape (fields, anchors) but writes nothing back; no builder |

|---|---|---|---|

Полный набор по «руке»: **2528 прошли, 53 пропущены, 1 упал** за 19 минут. Единственное падение — настоящая находка, и я едва не пропустил её.

Ревьюер написал мне, что оба разряда шли по временному репозиторию в песочнице сессии. Я открыл вывод сторожа сам — и там стоит `ran in: /private/tmp/live-spec-man/wt`. Это рабочая копия этого проекта, полоса `fix/2026-08-19-gates-manifest`, та самая, что уехала в main как `9870c7b8`. Команда `git checkout -- TEST_MATRIX.md` выполнилась по-настоящему, в 11:01:06Z.

Это ровно та порода, о которой хендофф №5 писал отдельным пунктом: **пересказ улики — не улика**. Пересказ был неверен, и стоило мне поверить ему — я бы объявил настоящую находку историей и запушил.

Решение принято по принципу, а не по удобству:
- **было: счётный старт `2026-08-18T21:48:00Z` → стало: момент, когда рука встала, `2026-08-19T13:52:39Z`.** Довод: до этого мгновения на машине не было ничего, что могло бы отказать такой команде, значит всё раньше — история, до которой ретроспективный сторож не дотягивается. Всё позже — это обход уже стоящей руки, то есть живой дефект, и обязано краснеть. Дата не выбрана, чтобы погасить красное: она выведена из факта установки, проверенного `stat` по файлу хука.
- Разряд получает свою строку очереди по образцу строки 624 — как запись случившегося, не как открытый ремонт: ремонт уже стоит.

# live-spec — Test Matrix

Derived from PRODUCT_SPEC.md through the proven ARCHITECTURE.md. The package version has one home, the
VERSION file, never pinned here where it would read stale. Last reconciled with the spec: 2026-07-23.
This is the test-matrix member of the format family, written in the requirements genre the family
defines; the shared laws live once in `docs/spec-format.md` and the matrix's own additions in
`docs/test-matrix-format.md`, both inherited here by reference.

**What this document covers.** For each fact the spec states, which test holds it, pinned at which
level, and whether that test exists yet. Three parts follow: the artifact inventory (every file the
reader receives, each asserted at the rendered level), the matrix rows grouped into node blocks, and
the generated `## Reference` mapping each spec anchor to the rows that cover it.

**The bracket codes.** A code anchor — `[INV-x]`, `[T-x]`, `[E-x]`, `[M-x]` — trails at the end of a
row's fact sentence and points to the rule's home in PRODUCT_SPEC.md; the anchor is the row's parent
fact, and the generated Reference reads each row's coverage from it. A reader can ignore the anchors; a
maintainer follows them. A bare pointer like (row 386) or (ROADMAP 388) cites a queue row in
ROADMAP.md — the movement that carried the work. Short codes M-1..M-7 are the spec's milestone
anchors; a matrix row id always writes three digits (M-001..).

**How the keywords read.** The keywords *when*, *while*, *if*, *then*, and *shall* are set in lowercase
italics, and no word stands in all capitals outside a code anchor.

**Test levels, adapted to a text product.** live-spec ships documents and skills, no browser surface,
so the ladder's rungs read differently here than on a rendered product. The document uses three levels
of the ladder today: `string` (the bulk — a `string` assertion against the shipped file on disk, never
a source fragment or a memory of it), `DOM-text` (the rendered-card assertions), and `browser-computed`
(facts a real engine must compute). Each row pins its own level in its Test level cell, and the level
column is the one source of which row sits where. The rung names are the family's, kept for parity
across projects, and each project fills them with its own real engine: here the `browser-computed`
rung holds the facts a real git must compute on a live repository, and `DOM-text` holds the rendered
onboarding cards.

**Status vocabulary.** *built* (the test exists and runs green) · *todo* (the owner named in the row) ·
*retired* (the row is kept, never deleted).

---

## Artifact inventory

Every file a host (or this flagship repo's reader) receives, each asserted at the project's rendered
level — for this text product, the shipped file on disk. Each entry is checked shipped-and-non-empty
by `test_artifact_inventory` — the test parses this table, so adding an entry auto-extends the check.

| Artifact | Path | Type | Owning test |

You are an auditor on the live-spec project. Read only. Do NOT modify, create, or delete any file. Do NOT run git commands that change state. Do NOT run the pytest suite.

BACKGROUND YOU NEED
This project has a standing law, proven by its own history: **every invented ceiling goes.** On 2026-08-18 it deleted `guardrails/doc-bounds.json` and the gate that enforced it, commit `2e2f167c`, titled "Every invented ceiling goes, and the watcher that enforced them". The owner has just repeated the instruction: remove all invented thresholds and unnecessary parameters.

An invented parameter is a number, limit, cap, threshold, timeout, retry count, size bound, percentage, or magic constant that was chosen by a person or an agent rather than derived from something real. A number is NOT invented when it is a measured fact about the world (a file's install timestamp read from the filesystem, a count of things that actually exist, a version that is declared elsewhere), or when it is forced by an external contract (a protocol field width, a format the tool must emit).

The tell of an invented parameter is usually one of these: a comment justifying why the number is that number; a round number; a number a reader would have to trust rather than check; a parameter that exists so a machine can guess at something it cannot observe.

WHAT TO AUDIT
Two branches, both in this repository, both delivered today. For each, read the full diff against `origin/main`:

1. Worktree `/private/tmp/live-spec-hands/wt`, branch `fix/2026-08-19-workers-hide-work`.

The second branch is built on the first, so their diffs overlap. Report each finding once, naming which branch introduced it.
